[The Messy Desktop Problem]{.slide-title}

```
Desktop/
├── bee_data_final.csv
├── bee_data_final_FINAL.csv
```

## {#cost data-menu-title="Cost"}

[The Cost of Disorganization]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
**Scenario 1:** Reviewer requests changes  
→ Can't figure out what you did 6 months ago

**Scenario 2:** Lab partner needs your code  
→ `Error: cannot open 'C:/Users/YourName/...'`

**Scenario 3:** Journal requires code deposit  
→ Week writing documentation for code you barely remember

**All solved by:** Well-organized projects
:::

---

## {#what-is data-menu-title="What Is Project"}

[What Is a Project?]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
**A self-contained folder containing everything needed to reproduce an analysis**

**Self-contained** = All files in one folder  
**Everything needed** = Data, scripts, outputs, documentation  
**Organized logically** = Clear structure  
**For someone else** = Collaborator, reviewer, future-you

**Projects answer:**
1. What data? → `data/` folder
2. What did I do? → documented in scripts
3. What did I produce? → saved in `figures/`
:::

---

## {#good-structure data-menu-title="Good Structure"}

[A Well-Organized Project]{.slide-title}

:::{.code-text}
```
bee_diversity_analysis/
├── data/
│   ├── raw/                # Original, untouched
│   └── processed/          # Cleaned data
├── scripts/
│   ├── 01_clean_data.R     # Numbered = order
│   ├── 02_calculate_richness.R
│   └── 03_make_figures.R
├── figures/
├── README.md               # START HERE
└── bee_diversity.Rproj     # RStudio project
```
:::

:::{.body-text}
✅ Clear hierarchy | ✅ Protected raw data | ✅ Numbered scripts | ✅ Self-documenting
:::

---

## {#raw-vs-processed data-menu-title="Raw vs Processed"}

[Raw vs. Processed Data]{.slide-title}

:::{.code-text}
```
data/
├── raw/         # What you started with
└── processed/   # What you created
```
:::

:::{.body-text}
**Raw data** = from field/lab/instrument  
→ **Never changes. Ever.**

**Processed data** = created by cleaning raw data  
→ **Result of running a script**

**Golden rule:**  
Delete processed data and regenerate it by running scripts.

**From now on: Raw data is read-only. All changes in code.**
:::

## {#paths-intro data-menu-title="Paths Introduction"}

[Why Paths Matter]{.slide-title}

![Artwork by Allison Horst](../../images/allison-horst-pathways.png){width=80% fig-align="center"}

:::{.body-text}
**The problem:** Hardcoding file locations breaks everything
:::

---

## {#paths-explained data-menu-title="Paths Explained"}

[Absolute vs. Relative Paths]{.slide-title}

![Artwork by Allison Horst](../../images/allison-horst-pathways.png){width=65% fig-align="center"}

:::{.body-text}
**The broken cube** = `setwd()` and absolute paths (fragile!)  
**The strong cube** = R Projects (robust!)  
**The skilled cube** = `here` package (even better!)
:::

---

## {#paths-bad data-menu-title="Absolute Paths Bad"}

[Absolute Paths (BAD)]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
**This only works on MY computer:**
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

# BAD - Absolute path
data <- read.csv("/Users/gretchen/Desktop/bee_analysis/data/raw/bees.csv")
```

:::{.body-text}
**Error on your computer:**
```
Error: cannot open file '/Users/gretchen/Desktop/...': 
No such file or directory
```

**Why?** You don't have a user named "gretchen"
:::

---

## {#paths-good data-menu-title="Relative Paths Good"}

[Relative Paths (GOOD)]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
**This works on ANYONE's computer:**
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

# GOOD - Relative path
data <- read.csv("data/raw/bees.csv")
```

:::{.body-text}
**Why it works:**  
"Starting from the project folder, go into `data/`, then `raw/`, read `bees.csv`"

Works on any computer, any operating system!
:::

---

## {#paths-scenario data-menu-title="Path Scenarios"}

[Why Relative Paths Save Your Life]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
**With absolute paths:**

1. Analysis at school: `C:/Users/Student/.../data.csv`
2. Work at home → **ERROR** (different path)
3. Fix all paths manually
4. Back at school → **ERROR** (wrong again)
5. Email advisor → **ERROR** (doesn't have your folders)

**With relative paths:**

1. Analysis at school: `"data/raw/data.csv"`
2. Work at home → ✅ **Works**
3. Back at school → ✅ **Works**
4. Email advisor → ✅ **Works**
:::

## {#rstudio-demo-2 data-menu-title="Demo - RStudio"}

[Creating the RStudio Project]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
**Step 3:** In RStudio:  
`File > New Project > Existing Directory`

**Step 4:** Create script `scripts/01_load_data.R`
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

# Load water quality data
water <- read.csv("data/raw/water_samples.csv")

# Check it loaded
head(water)
```

:::{.body-text}
**Notice:** Path is `"data/raw/..."` not full path!
:::

## {#rstudio-demo-3 data-menu-title="Demo - Test Portability"}

[Testing Portability]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
**Step 5:** The test

1. Close RStudio
2. Move entire project folder to Desktop (or anywhere!)
3. Double-click `.Rproj` file
4. Run script again

**Result:** ✅ Still works!

**Why?** Relative paths are relative to project root
:::

## {#readme-importance data-menu-title="README Importance"}

[Every Project Needs a README]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
**README.md is the first thing anyone reads**

Answers four questions:
1. What is this project about?
2. What data does it use?
3. How do I run the analysis?
4. Who do I contact?

**Without README:** Confusion and frustration  
**With README:** Clear path forward
:::

---

## {#readme-bad data-menu-title="README Bad"}

[Bad README Example]{.slide-title}

:::{.code-text}
```markdown
# My Project

This is my analysis.
```
:::

:::{.body-text}
**This tells you nothing:**
- What's the research question?
- What data?
- How to run it?
- Who made it?

**Useless!**
:::

---

## {#readme-good data-menu-title="README Good"}

[Good README Example]{.slide-title}

:::{.code-text}
```markdown
# Bee Diversity in Urban Gardens

## Overview
Analysis of bee species richness across 45 urban garden 
sites in San Francisco, May–August 2023.

Research question: Does richness differ between 
community gardens and private yards?

## Data
- Raw: `data/raw/bee_surveys.csv` (field surveys)
- Processed: `data/processed/bee_clean.csv` 

## Scripts (run in order)
1. `01_clean_data.R` - Removes incomplete surveys
2. `02_calculate_richness.R` - Rarefied richness
3. `03_make_figures.R` - Generates figures

## Contact
Gretchen LeBuhn (lebuhn@sfsu.edu)
```
:::

## {#checklist data-menu-title="Checklist"}

[Project Structure Checklist]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
**Every project needs:**

**Folders:**
- [ ] `data/raw/` — original, never modified
- [ ] `data/processed/` — cleaned/transformed
- [ ] `scripts/` — numbered if order matters
- [ ] `figures/` — all plots

**Files:**
- [ ] `.Rproj` file
- [ ] `README.md`
- [ ] Descriptive file names

**Code:**
- [ ] Relative paths only
- [ ] Scripts numbered
- [ ] Comments explain decisions
:::

---

## {#mistakes data-menu-title="Common Mistakes"}

[Common Mistakes to Avoid]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
❌ **Working outside project folder**  
Quick plot saved to Desktop → lost forever

❌ **Using absolute paths**  
`C:/Users/You/...` → won't work for others

❌ **Editing raw data**  
Fix typo in Excel, save → reproducibility destroyed

❌ **No README**  
6 months later, no idea what anything does

❌ **Too many versions**  
`analysis_final_REALLY_final_v3.R`
:::

---

## {#git-preview data-menu-title="Git Preview"}

[Git Setup Preview]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
**This week's activity:** Set up Git and GitHub

**Git** = Version control system  
Tracks every change to files

**GitHub** = Website to host repositories

**Why?** One file (`analysis.R`) with all versions tracked

No more:
- `analysis_final_v3.R`
- `analysis_final_REALLY_final.R`

**We'll cover Git concepts in Week 4**
:::

## {#summary data-menu-title="Summary"}

[Key Concepts to Remember]{.slide-title}

:::{.body-text}
1. **Projects = unit of scientific work**

2. **Good structure = reproducibility**

3. **Raw data never changes** — modifications in code

4. **Relative paths = portable code**

5. **Documentation required**

6. **Organization IS doing science**

**Questions? → Discussion board or office hours**
